title: Private Credit, Private Markets and Their Drivers

maps.tested: Two readings rated Very Important, one in Investment Management, one in Current Issues. Reported twice by name in exam recalls.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'private credit', listed twice in the same consolidated sheet. The examinable material is the growth drivers, the bank-disintermediation story, the valuation opacity and the financial-stability concerns. Cheap marks if read; zero if skipped.

vardeezReading: IM-10: Very Important, with the note "Private Credit Risks". IM-11: Important, with the note "Private Market Investment Structures, Private Equity Performance Measures: IRR, MOIC, PME, Co-Investing: Benefits and Risks". CI-3: Very Important, with the note "Solve book-wise Current Issues questions; anything can show up." IM-13 (see also): untiered, with the note "Lo 95.a and LO 95.b both are Imp".

selectors.name: Private credit growth drivers, BIS regression
selectors.what: The four drivers of private credit growth (low policy rates, low banking-sector efficiency measured by the FI index, higher bank regulatory stringency, rising corporate leverage) and how the BIS regression (45 countries, 2010 to 2019, new private credit origination) ranks them by economic effect: FI index decline about +33%, policy rate decline about +12%, regulatory stringency rise about +2% to 4%, corporate leverage under 1%.

selectors.name: Bank disintermediation, private credit vs bank loans
selectors.what: Why banks retreated after 2007 to 2009 and private credit funds took over lending to riskier mid-sized firms, and how private credit loans compare with bank loans (flexible terms, tailored covenants, fast execution). The cost of equity, cost of debt and leverage story for US banks vs BDCs: BDC cost of equity below banks', cost of debt marginally above, banks' funding advantage narrowed by about 250 bp in 2010 to 2019, equally from higher bank cost of equity and BDC leverage, with cost of debt playing almost no role.

selectors.name: Valuation opacity, stale marks, NAV metrics
selectors.what: Why private credit valuations are opaque (few comparables, infrequent valuations, no secondary market, no mandated method) and what follows: stale marks overstate value and returns, inflate manager fees, and defer and then bunch losses; NAV can differ from price for several quarters; more frequent valuation is not automatically better.

selectors.name: Financial-stability concerns and IMF policy fixes
selectors.what: The IMF's assessment of private credit risks to financial stability (credit, liquidity, leverage, interconnectedness, conduct, underwriting; judged moderate today but untested by a serious downturn) and the matching policy recommendations (bank-like monitoring, closed-end structures and liquidity tools, leverage reporting and stress tests, valuation oversight, data sharing, conflict disclosure).

selectors.name: PE performance: IRR, TVPI, DPI, PME
selectors.what: Compute or compare the private equity performance measures: DPI = distributions / paid-in, RVPI = residual value (NAV) / paid-in, TVPI = DPI + RVPI, IRR as the rate solving the sum of cash flows over (1 + r)^t = 0 (calls negative, distributions positive), and PME as the sum of distributions discounted at index returns over the sum of calls discounted at index returns (above 1 means the fund outperformed the index). Also which measure is least manipulable, and the advantages and weaknesses of each.
selectors.theory: What each measure captures and its limits: IRR is time-sensitive, not risk adjusted, assumes reinvestment at the IRR and is inflated by credit lines that delay calls; TVPI ignores time and cannot be annualised; DPI uses realised cash only and is least manipulable; TVPI and RVPI depend on NAV; PME needs both legs index-adjusted and is benchmark sensitive; all use paid-in, not committed, capital.

selectors.name: Private markets structures, co-investing, intermediated vehicles
selectors.what: Compare the investment structures (direct investment, private funds, funds of funds, managed accounts, SPVs, securitization) by involvement, diversification, cost and control; the pros and cons of co-investing (reduced or no fee and carry, control, adverse selection, concentration, passive role); and the benefits and challenges of intermediated vehicles (fees, principal-agent risk, blind pool risk, illiquidity, conflicts).

notSelected: IM-10 a and b (characteristics, return and growth profile of private credit), IM-11 a (motivations) and IM-11 d (risks of private markets and their measures), and CI-3 a (structure of private credit funds and global growth patterns) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer, and the see-also reading IM-13 (distress symptoms and remedies, flagged by Vardeez only as LO 95.a and 95.b being important) has no shape and is not listed among this topic's learning objectives.
